label: Sought the weakest premise excluding the part-free two-root model and tested its independence
summary: Sought the weakest premise excluding the part-free two-root model and tested its independence. Given individuation, the first-mover adapter and every-perfection, distinct first movers can only have one act profile and different natures, and at-most-one is equivalent to act-determines-nature and to first-movers-share-nature; so those two conditions are not independent of uniqueness given those premises, and the #715 content bundle is strictly stronger than the first. The non-equivalent form tried is UnlimitedBeingsShareNature: it does not use every-perfection, each of five hypotheses is needed by a control, and it exceeds uniqueness on a single-mover carrier. Its first-mover instance is still not independent, and it is vacuous at every pair with a limited member, so ordinary pluralities give it no instance. Rejected: treating ordinary limited pairs as inductive support for the root pair; treating formal independence of the universal as an independent defense; using the intelligences of De ente c.3 as a counterexample, since that passage denies them omnimoda simplicitas through esse other than quiddity, which is a limiting principle here. Details in docs/notes/necessary-simple-plurality.md.
blocker: Defend the bridge, or a replacement, on grounds that do not reduce to its first-mover instance and that answer the different-whole-essence rival; separately defend applying first-mover premises to a selected necessary underived individual. The part-free model survives every hypothesis but the bridge.
